newsitem.title: USA: Mellon to buy pension money management firm.
newsitem.headline: Mellon to buy pension money management firm.

text.p: Mellon Bank Corp. said Monday it agreed to buy Buck Consultants Inc., a New York-based firm that provides administrative and consulting services for corporate pension and benefit plans with assets totaling approximately $400 billion.
Terms were not disclosed. Officials from both companies declined to comment on a purchase price but said the transaction should close in next year's second quarter.
Under the agreement, the privately held Buck will become a Mellon subsidiary and keep its current management team, Mellon said. No layoffs are expected as a result of the transaction.
Mellon's stock was trading at $73.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in late afternoon, unchanged from Friday's close.

Buck provides pension and health and welfare actuarial services, and employee benefits, compensation and human resources consulting and administrative services to approximately 5,000 worldwide clients. The firm has offices in 16 countries.

W. Keith Smith, Mellon's vice chairman, said the acquisition should position Mellon as a leader in the growing field of managing pension and benefits plans for other companies, also known as benefits outsourcing.

"We see it as a major growth area ... it was led by the major corporations but we expect it to spread to the mid-size and small companies," he said. "Over time, clearly it will be accretive to earnings."
Smith said using outside firms to manage benefits was generally cheaper for companies than in-house management and could produce better benefits packages for employees.
Joseph LoCicero, president and chief executive officer of Buck, said his company last year decided to expand its benefits outsourcing capabilities via a merger.
"We began a search for a compatible partner ... this transaction clearly is a strategic one for us," he said.
"Together, we have vast resources, leading-edge systems and technology, and the ability to deliver an integrated array of benefits-related services to the clients of both companies."

Buck posted revenues of $197 million for the fiscal year ended March 31, 1996, of which $50 million was generated by non-U.S. operations. It is the seventh largest benefits consultant in the United States and the eighth largest in the world, based on revenues.
Mellon expects to retain substantially all Buck employees following completion of the acquisition, and to add to total employment as the growth of the combined companies accelerates.
